speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me when your fever started and if the skin lesions appeared before or after you noticed the wrist pain? Also, have you had any recent insect bites or travel to a tropical region?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent camping trip in Minnesota and the sequence of symptoms, have you noticed any bull's-eye rash elsewhere on your body, and do you recall being bitten by a tick? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of a Minnesota camping trip, recent self-resolving monoarticular knee pain, and now violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the wrists is highly concerning for Lyme arthritis with secondary cutaneous involvement or a co-infection like Erythema Chronicum Migrans. Given the severity and your concern, I am ordering urgent imaging and serology. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, Lyme Serology (ELISA/Western Blot). REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the left wrist, MRI of the left knee if available. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Lyme Disease
